prompt: A clean, straight-on photograph of a printed intravenous-infusion label wrapped on a ward IV fluid BAG hanging on a drip stand, plain print on a white label. The infusion is a weight-based drug order: patient weight 31 kg, drug dose 45 mg per kilogram, drug supplied at a concentration of 2.5 mg per mL, the whole dose to run over 5 hours using a giving-set with a drop factor of 15 drops per mL (gtt/mL). The label has a bold field 'SET RATE (gtt/min):' followed by the single whole-number drip rate the nurse should set. Work it out in order: total drug in mg = dose per kg x weight; volume to infuse in mL = total mg / concentration; then convert that volume and the time to a flow in drops per minute using the drop factor (drops = volume x drop factor; minutes = hours x 60) and round to the nearest whole drop per minute. Print that whole number there. Also print the weight, dose, concentration, time and drop factor as reference lines. Print only these numbers; make the SET RATE value large and legible. No working or formula on the label.
